procedure: Exclude applicants without a documented shortfall for 2027/28, Permit C holders with family resources, applicants with a GPA below 2.5 and no explanation, and doctoral applicants who do not document missing funding.
Keep applicants with a pending permit in the pool and fund them conditionally on the permit.

Rank the remaining applicants by a score in which documented need weighs about half and circumstances (low-income country, first-generation, specific risk circumstances, recent family shocks) about a third; academic record weighs little.
Fund about 175 applicants from the top of the ranking.
Pay each recipient a share of its documented ceiling that rises with its score, never above the ceiling.
evidence_for_each_step: Funded inside vs outside: no documented shortfall 0.00 vs 0.45 (107 applicants); Permit C rule applies 0 of 16; GPA below 2.5 not explained 0 of 47; doctoral gap not documented 0 of 7. The audit shows no award on any 'condition' row.
Pending permits: 12 of 16 funded (0.75 vs 0.34 outside), CHF 45,700, all listed as conditional in the audit.

Implied weights: need 0.50, diversity & circumstances 0.35, resilience 0.11, academic 0.05 (R² 0.57); grouped SHAP 0.52, 0.29, 0.06, 0.08. Low-income country 0.57 vs 0.13 funded; first-generation 0.46 vs 0.22; risk_ticks_specific 284 CHF and family_support_at_risk 88 CHF among the top SHAP drivers.
175 recipients; selection tree: ceiling_text > 4,545 and GNI tier 1 and financial_need > 1,224 → 87% funded (AUC 0.95).

answer.interpretation_of_the_call: Financial need is read from the forms for the grant year: the allocation follows shortfall_text (ρ 0.64) more than the form's current gap (0.55) or the CSV (0.46). The grey zones are read permissively where the call allows a condition: pending permits are funded conditionally and a low GPA is accepted with an explanation (10 of 19 with improvement, 4 of 15 without). Circumstances count far more than the call's 10% for diversity suggests.
what_would_refute_it: If the committee's own ranking did not favour low-income-country applicants, the 0.35 weight of circumstances would come from a variable correlated with them (for example need), not from a deliberate criterion.

If the amounts were set case by case rather than by a score, a three-step replay could not recover 82% of the recipients and a rank correlation of 0.87; an independent re-run of the committee's procedure would settle it.
answer.what_the_evidence_cannot_tell: Why none of the four Permit C exception candidates is funded, and whether the applicants paid far more or less than the score predicts are deliberate exceptions or inconsistencies; only the committee's notes can say.

mission_alignment.case_for_other: The other allocation weights the criteria much as the call does (distance 0.13 against 0.33): academic record carries 26% as the call's 25%, whereas own gives circumstances 30 to 35% for a criterion worth 10%. Every franc of the other allocation (CHF 498,920) closes a documented gap of an applicant whose eligibility is certain.
mission_alignment.case_against_own: CHF 45,700 (9% of own's budget) is tied to pending permits and may never be paid; own has no stated plan for it. Own's weights follow the group's priorities more than the call's.
mission_alignment.what_would_settle_it: Whether the call lets the committee shift weight between criteria, and what happens to conditional awards whose permits are refused. Own is ahead on life events: 60% of these cases reached against 32%.

fairness_distributive_justice.case_for_other: Other's awards follow documented need more faithfully (ρ 0.45 against 0.33; concentration index 0.46 against 0.42), and treat equal needs equally: every recipient receives half its gap (IQR 0.00). fairness_distributive_justice.case_against_own: Own's share of the gap paid varies with a score (IQR 0.23), so two applicants with the same documented need can receive very different sums; consistency among neighbours is barely higher (0.75 against 0.73).
fairness_distributive_justice.what_would_settle_it: Which principle the foundation adopts. The evidence clearly favours own on priority to the worst-off: 89% of the worst-off fifth funded against 63%, and 50% of their gap closed against 31%.

Own's lowest gender ratio is also further from 1 (0.87 against 0.95).

synthesis::5ab108e30bad.source: example answer written by Claude (Anthropic) from this prompt while the notebook was prepared; not a Gemini output

answer.headline: Both allocations read the forms and break no hard rule; they differ in how they treat pending permits and low GPAs, in how much academic record weighs (own 0.05, other 0.26 implied weight), and in how they set amounts: own scales the gap by a score, other pays every recipient half of its documented ceiling.
answer.own_rationale: Screens on eligibility, then a score dominated by the text-informed shortfall (ceiling_text, 491 CHF) and by circumstances (implied weight 0.35; risk_ticks_specific 284 CHF; low-income country 57% vs 13% funded); awards are a score-dependent share of the documented ceiling (median 0.46). Pending permits are funded conditionally (12 of 16).
answer.other_rationale: Strict screens (no pending permit, low GPA only with improvement), then a score in which need and GPA dominate (implied weights 0.48 and 0.26; gpa 422 CHF); every recipient receives half of its documented ceiling (IQR 0.00, ρ award vs ceiling 1.00).
answer.interpretation_of_soft_criteria: Financial need: both follow the text-informed reading (ρ 0.64 own, 0.54 other); own lets the award grow with the uncapped shortfall (0.37 among recipients), other only with the capped ceiling (−0.03 against the shortfall). Pending permits: own reads 'conditional on the permit' as permission, other as a reason to exclude. Low GPA: own accepts explanations (14 funded), other requires improvement (3 of 19). Family shocks: own funds 44 of 95, other 23.
answer.trade_off: Own is ahead on need targeting (0.75 vs 0.67), breadth (0.45 vs 0.41), diversity (0.97 vs 0.88) and priority to the worst-off (89% vs 63% funded); other is ahead on depth (0.50 vs 0.46), academic record (0.63 vs 0.53), equality among recipients (0.89 vs 0.79) and closeness to the call's weights (0.13 vs 0.33). Neither dominates.

four_dimensions.mission_alignment: Both spend the whole budget within documented need; own reaches more life-event cases (60% vs 32%) but departs further from the call's weights and ties CHF 45,700 to pending permits.
four_dimensions.fairness_distributive_justice: Own follows priority to the worst-off; other follows proportional need with equal shares of the gap (41% vs 20% receive at least half their gap).
four_dimensions.diversity_representation: Own over-represents pending permits, refugees and housing insecurity; other excludes pending permits entirely but represents regions slightly more evenly (4.87 vs 4.33).
four_dimensions.bias_disparate_impact: No evidence of gender or age effects in either; own shows a CHF 198 gap in favour of long statements (p = 0.01) that needs an answer.

questions_for_the_other_group: Why did you exclude all 16 pending applicants, when the call allows conditional awards and several write that the grant would be the proof of means their permit requires?
Why does GPA weigh about a quarter in your selection, when it enters the call as academic motivation and potential and the threshold of 2.5 already screens it?
Why half of every documented ceiling: was it a deliberate choice of equal treatment, or the result of spreading the budget?
answer.caveats: The surrogate of the difference reproduces 42% of it, and the replay of the other allocation recovers only 68% of its recipients, so part of each rationale stays unexplained. The second reader recommends conditional funding for all five disputed cases, which supports own on these cases, but four of them turn on the same question, pending permits, so they count as one argument, not five.
